sourceChecks.claim: Core components verifies primary-key-addressed items. Redis persistence primary followup confirms persistence is configurable, including disabled persistence; access model alone does not imply crash survival or a cache-only role.

GetItem verifies retrieval by key and absent Item versus operation errors. PutItem and WorkingWithItems primary followups verify complete replacement and deletion, supporting the example trace and response/absence distinction.

IAM conditions verifies explicit permissions restricting item access by identity and key. Names alone confer no permission; the namespace diagram and constrained separator example prevent the stated identity collisions.

SecondaryIndexes verifies alternate query keys and automatic maintenance on add/modify/delete. Scan primary followup confirms inspected-entry reads precede filtering; index lookup adds a maintained data structure.

Condition expressions attach conditions to writes and reject unmet conditions. OptimisticLocking and WorkingWithItems primary followups verify current-version checks, version advancement, failed stale writes and reread/update recovery. ReadConsistency explicitly permits modification immediately after a read, refuting separate-check protection.

Error handling verifies uncertain single-item write outcomes and conditional/idempotent retry handling. WorkingWithItems verifies atomic counter retries can overcount; TransactWriteItems verifies atomic actions and same-token/idempotency-window limits, supporting scoped duplicate protection.

TTL verifies delayed background deletion and expired entries pending deletion. Redis eviction primary followup verifies configured memory-pressure removal, distinct from expiry. These sources support the absence of retention, automatic refresh or exact-time business-execution guarantees.

Partition-key design verifies load distribution matters and per-partition capacity limits remain. ReadConsistency primary followup distinguishes durable successful writes from stale eventual reads; Redis persistence verifies crash-survival settings vary.

NoSQL design verifies choosing around known access patterns and expense of queries outside them. Checked scan/index/partition sources support extra reads, maintenance and uneven-load limits; the lesson correctly requires workload-specific measurement.
